summary: A runnable local prototype of the AccountSignal Portfolio Page using Citizens source JSON plus equivalent Commerce Bank and Synovus fixtures.

questions.question: Which language should the portfolio frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed React application with straightforward component contracts.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Plain JavaScript frontend with fewer type constraints.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is a good fit for shared public and subscriber response models.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and interaction style should the prototype use?

options.label: React with Vite
options.description: Fast local development with a component-based portfolio page.

options.label: Vue with Vite
options.description: Component-based alternative for the browser UI.

questions.rationale: The prototype needs a browser-runnable UI with filters, detail views and mode switching.

questions.question: Which frontend behaviors should the prototype demonstrate?
questions.recommendedChoice: Portfolio list, institution and domain filters, search, public signal cards, gated opportunity teaser, and subscriber/demo opportunity detail
questions.answer: Portfolio list, institution and domain filters, search, public signal cards, gated opportunity teaser, and subscriber/demo opportunity detail
questions.rationale: These behaviors are explicit in the requested prototype scope and supplied implementation approach.

questions.question: Which language should the local portfolio API use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Self-contained API with shared types and fixture loading.

options.label: Python
options.description: Small API service with Python-based fixture transformation.

questions.rationale: A single TypeScript toolchain keeps the local prototype straightforward and self-contained.

questions.question: Which backend framework and API style should the prototype use?

options.label: Express REST API
options.description: Minimal local API for institutions, signals, filters and gated opportunity detail.

options.label: Fastify REST API
options.description: Lightweight alternative with schema-oriented request handling.

questions.rationale: The requested experience needs a small HTTP boundary without production infrastructure.

questions.question: Which backend behaviors should the prototype demonstrate?
questions.recommendedChoice: Fixture ingestion and normalization, institution and signal listing, query filtering, public-safe projections, demo entitlement mode, and opportunity detail retrieval
questions.answer: Fixture ingestion and normalization, institution and signal listing, query filtering, public-safe projections, demo entitlement mode, and opportunity detail retrieval
questions.rationale: The API must enforce the public/subscriber boundary rather than relying on browser-only hiding.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores should the local prototype use?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Load committed JSON fixtures into memory at API startup.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Use a local file database for persistence and query experiments.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The requested prototype is self-contained and explicitly excludes production deployment or external secrets.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in for application API features?

options.label: No
options.description: Use an explicit local Public/Demo mode toggle to demonstrate entitlement behavior without identity infrastructure.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Add a local sign-in flow for subscriber access.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The request asks for subscriber/demo mode, not production identity or credential integration.

constraints: Use supplied Citizens JSON as source/fixture
Provide equivalent fixtures for Commerce Bank and Synovus
Do not implement application code during planning
